messages.content: The response must contain between 77 and 99 words. Patient says their neck feels stiff and swollen around throat area and throat feels sore. As a doctor, you can see no signs of swelling, and it's confirmed not to be a respiratory infection. What are the possible causes from the data you can gather?

message.content: Possible causes include cervical muscle tension or strain, cervical spine irritation, trigger points, or posture-related neck stiffness. Referred pain from the upper neck, TMJ tension, or esophageal/laryngeal spasm can mimic throat swelling and soreness. Laryngopharyngeal reflux, GERD, postnasal drip, or mild non-respiratory pharyngeal irritation may cause throat fullness without visible swelling. Anxiety or somatic symptoms can heighten sensation of tightness. Non-respiratory causes include dental or oral pathology, medication effects, or thyroid irritation if tenderness exists. Check exam findings, fever, swallowing, voice change, and duration.
